subject.title: fix(cron): preserve future one-shots during manual runs

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this narrow future-slot ownership repair, or consolidate the remaining manual-run semantics under the broader origin-based approach proposed in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/83933?
rationale: Both branches address the same destructive operator workflow but choose different ownership boundaries; the protected maintainer label and overlapping open PR require an explicit owner choice rather than an automated supersession judgment.

options.title: Adopt the narrow repair
options.body: Land this focused timestamp-based preservation path after it has attached redacted live CLI or gateway evidence for all stated manual-run outcomes.

options.title: Consolidate on run origins
options.body: Pause this PR and ask the authors to converge on the broader explicit-origin design if maintainers want one model for all manual and watcher-triggered scheduler ownership.

recommendation.title: Adopt the narrow repair
recommendation.body: Land this focused timestamp-based preservation path after it has attached redacted live CLI or gateway evidence for all stated manual-run outcomes.

likelyOwner.reason: The current author is the closest available routing candidate for reconciling this focused patch with the overlapping implementation and requested test evidence.
